doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Christmas in Washington with his musical nieces
summary: Powell describes his young nieces studying violin by the Suzuki method, the Christmas pageant, and a busy few days of gigs and filming.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. And it’s amazing to see at three years old. Man, I had the greatest time. I wish we had — well we’ll talk off the record about my Christmas holidays what I slipped to them. And another thing, since they’re taking lessons — oh well their mother, they work with flash cards. Every morning at 8:30, their mother is teaching them at home. So she makes it fun. Flash cards are those cards, you know what flash cards, but I’m speaking for the people that don’t know, it’s a card with a staff on it and a note, but not the name of the note. So with their mother, she plays if they get it in a minute it’s theirs, if they don’t it’s hers. So she makes a game out of it man, and all of this stuff, oh man, it’s just so slick. Well I covered a lot of bases when I was in Washington over the Christmas holidays, because first of all I got there, I left here at 7 o’clock in the morning. I got there in time to go to 5 o’clock mass, at which these same two young ladies performed. One was a sheep and the other one was an angel. The one who wants to be a singer was an angel singing on stage. Oh man it was so funny. I hope this is not too far away from the point, but the one who was a sheep couldn’t understand — she says, “Uncle Benny, I’m kind of worried about my line.” She said, “When I tell my line to people they laugh and I can’t understand why.” I said, “What’s your line?” She said, “Baaaa.” Oh man, and it was all I could do to keep a straight face because she was seriously into it. Anyway when I would take my horn out to practice, they just reach for their violin automatically. It’s not like come play with Uncle Benny. They think we’re all supposed to play “Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star” with that Suzuki method.
[scats] My kids did it too. BC: You know the deal.

Pepperoni pizza, isn’t it? BC: Because at first, so I knew “Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star,” we played through that already. So I said, “What else do you guys know? And one of them said, “Chuckle Chuckle Stops Up.” And I said, “I don’t know that,” and I said, “play it for me.” Oh man. And then there was another one, “Run Mamma, Daddy.” Anyway I had a great time with them. I got there and then we had a great Christmas. I don’t have time to really tell you how funny, but the next day I had a gig in Washington at a club called Schwinns, with a local rhythm section, oh just great guys. I’m terrible for names. Alan Johnson I know was on piano. A nice rhythm section they just had to put together that I had the date

on. The following day I got up and did a shoot just like this for my niece who was putting together this footage. And I got on the bus that evening and in about three or four days I covered all forms of media.
